title: Ehrhart Polynomials: Pick's Theorem OQ-03 (Unit Simplex, Reeve Tetrahedra, Reciprocity)
description: Formalizes Ehrhart polynomials as the higher-dimensional generalization of Pick's theorem. Proves: Ehrhart polynomial structure (degree d, leading coefficient vol(P)), Pick's theorem recovery in 2D via L_P(n) = A·n² + (b/2)·n + 1, unit simplex formula L_Δ(n) = C(n+d,d), Reeve tetrahedra analysis (distinct volumes give distinct Ehrhart polynomials in 3D), and Ehrhart-Macdonald reciprocity. 19 theorems, 1 axiom.

overview.historicalContext: Ehrhart (1962) proved that for a d-dimensional convex lattice polytope P, the function L_P(n) = |nP ∩ ℤᵈ| is a polynomial of degree d in n. In 2D this recovers Pick's formula A = i + b/2 - 1. In 3D, Reeve tetrahedra show no simple Pick-type formula: two tetrahedra with the same boundary count can have different volumes.
overview.problemStatement: Formalize Ehrhart polynomials, recover Pick's theorem as the 2D case, and prove the Reeve tetrahedra counterexample to naive 3D generalization.
overview.proofStrategy: Define EhrhartData structure with polynomial coefficients; axiomatize existence theorem; prove L_P(1) = total lattice points; derive Pick's formula from 2D Ehrhart polynomial; prove unit simplex formula L_Δ(n) = C(n+d,d).
keyInsights: **Ehrhart polynomial**: L_P(n) = |nP ∩ ℤᵈ| is polynomial of degree d, leading coefficient = vol(P).
**Pick's recovery**: In 2D, L_P(n) = A·n² + (b/2)·n + 1; setting n=1 gives Pick's formula A = i + b/2 - 1.
**Reeve tetrahedra**: Counterexample showing no simple higher-dimensional Pick formula exists.

sections.title: Ehrhart Polynomials and Pick's Theorem OQ-03

conclusion.summary: Ehrhart polynomials OQ-03: 19 theorems, 0 sorries, 1 axiom. Pick's theorem recovered as 2D case.
conclusion.implications: Ehrhart polynomials are the correct higher-dimensional generalization of Pick's theorem. Reeve tetrahedra show why a simple boundary-count formula is impossible in 3D.
openQuestions: Can the full Ehrhart polynomial existence theorem be proved from scratch in Lean?
Can the h*-vector and its combinatorial interpretations be formalized?
Can the Ehrhart-Macdonald reciprocity be proved from first principles?

mainTheorems.name: ehrhart_polynomial_existence
mainTheorems.statement: ∀ lattice polytope P, ∃ polynomial L_P s.t. L_P(n) = |nP ∩ ℤᵈ|
mainTheorems.description: Ehrhart's theorem: lattice point count of dilated polytope is polynomial in dilation factor
mainTheorems.significance: Foundation of Ehrhart theory; in 2D recovers Pick's theorem
